In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the classical and quantum CSM and RSvD systems with rational and trigonometric (or elliptic) potentials associated with the root systems of type A and BC.

the classical and quantum mechanical integrable systems with rational/trigometric potentials associated with root systems, their equilibrium positions and eigenfunctions, the classical and quantum factorization, shape invariance and their relations to the Askey scheme.
the following two topics; 1) Classical and quantum integrable multi-particle systems, 2) Classical and quantum orthogonal polynomials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the classical and quantum CSM systems and the classical and quantum RSvD are related by a simple deformation, and the orthogonal polynomials associated with these systems are related by the same deformation.

the equilibrium positions of classical CSM systems and the eigenfunction of quantum CSM systems, as well as those of classical RSvD and quantum RSvD, are all described by the classical and basic hypergeometric (quantum) orthogonal polynomials, respectively, which are all factorizable, shape invariant and belong to the same Askey-scheme.
all these systems have a common origin in a single algebra, the quantum group Uq(sl(2)), which has been known for a long time to be the algebra underlying the theory of the quantum groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the classical root systems (A,B,C,D) are the basic building blocks of the classical CSM systems, and that the classical root system A_n is the basic building block of the classical RSvD system.

the factorized Hamiltonians of the single-particle quantum Ruijsenaar-Schneider-von Diejen systems are deformation of the factorized Hamiltonian of the single-potential quantum Calogero-Schneider-Moser systems, and the equilibrium positions of multi-particle classical Ruijsenaaris-Schneider-vandiejen systems are deformation the equilibrium positions of classical Calogero-Moser-Schneider systems.
the CSM systems are the simplest examples of the RSvD systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the factorization and shape-invariance properties of these quantum Hamiltonians are inherited by the classical Hamiltonians.

the factorized Hamiltonians of the single-particle quantum Ruijsenaar-Schneider-vd Diejen systems can be expressed as a deformation of the factorized Hamiltonian of a single-particle quantum Calogero-Suthehrland-Moser system.
the eigenfunctions of these quantum systems are described by a single class of orthogonal polynomials, namely the basic hypergeometrics.
